📝 Notes
Feb 12, 2026
R&D daily sprint
Invited Amir Houieh Unbody io Noémi Biró Gabor Kerekes
Attachments R&D daily sprint Notes by Gemini 
Meeting records Transcript 
Summary
Noémi Biró shared user feedback on Cibil, which included concerns about it being triggering, lacking structure for grief processing, and the user's unawareness that Cibil's knowledge base was human-reviewed. Gabor Kerekes suggested that the team may have overestimated the common value of mental health chatbots, while Amir Houieh reported progress on the "unBody carefinder" project and finalized the decision with Gabor Kerekes and Noémi Biró to maintain the original unBody website structure, adding an explicit sentence about the pivot to "unBody lab" and agreeing to a three-day buffer period for internal review of new blog posts. Amir Houieh and Gabor Kerekes also discussed resolving website performance issues and refining design elements, including improving dark mode aesthetics and the challenges associated with the Minimum Credible Product for 'brain.'
Details
User Feedback on Cibil and Grief Processing Noémi Biró shared feedback from a user who found Cibil triggering a lot, even a year after their loss, and felt there was insufficient structure, making it "one more thing" they needed to figure out. The user also questioned how Cibil helps with grief processing, suggesting that the current approach—assuming journaling and chatting within Cibil equates to processing—may not work for everyone, highlighting a need for greater personalization. Noémi Biró also noted that Cibil should be proactive to encourage users to open the app (00:15:25).
Cibil Use Context and Tone The user spent about an hour using Cibil, needing to wait for time and space alone to engage with it, as they felt compelled to conceal their emotions from their 5-year-old daughter. The user ultimately found Cibil helpful due to its good tone and responses that acknowledged the non-linear, wave-like nature of grief (00:18:16). Gabor Kerekes suggested that the team might have been blind to the fact that not many people use chatbots for mental health, with only 1% or 1.5% of conversations on platforms like Claude being about such topics, contrasting with their assumption of its common value (00:19:33).
Knowledge Base and Chatbot Usage Noémi Biró mentioned that the user did not realize Cibil's knowledge base was reviewed by humans and not solely generated by AI. This raised a point about the UI's prominence and how prior experience with other AI applications influences user expectations regarding information sourcing (00:16:55). Noémi Biró also followed up with the user about their usage of other chat AI subscriptions (00:21:14).
Progress on unBody Projects Amir Houieh reported making good progress on the "unBody carefinder" project, which they are working to finalize for deployment and define new evaluation tests using real data. Amir Houieh clarified that this project is a legacy clean-up and not necessarily an "unBody lab" initiative. Amir Houieh also worked on improving the Minimum Credible Product (MCP) for 'brain' but expressed reservations about its necessity (00:22:32).
Rationale and Issues with the MCP for 'Brain' Gabor Kerekes explained that the MCP is needed for hosting the brain online, enabling its connection to cloud applications like Cloud Code and Cloud Desktop, and creating a shared memory layer between these applications. Amir Houieh noted a challenge with the MCP: the cloud environment does not explicitly commit to an endpoint for the brain, and it makes its own interpretation of the text rather than feeding the raw text to the brain (00:23:41) (00:26:13). Gabor Kerekes acknowledged that while it is not ideal, they found a different "basic memory" that can be hooked up to Cloud Desktop (00:25:09).
unBody Website Performance and Design Updates Gabor Kerekes resolved several performance issues with the unBody website, which were mainly occurring on mobile, particularly by removing a heavy blur on the background and replacing it with a gradient (00:27:28). The team discussed refining the dark mode, with Amir Houieh suggesting making shadows glow with the accent color instead of a shadow effect to improve the look (00:48:34).
Blog Post Management and Guidelines Gabor Kerekes and Amir Houieh discussed managing blog posts, deciding to keep articles that generate traffic and establish guidelines for publishing (00:28:53). To avoid unnecessary friction or micromanagement while ensuring shared vision, Amir Houieh suggested adding a disclaimer that each blog post represents the author's personal opinion (00:35:41). Noémi Biró proposed and the team agreed on a 3-day buffer period for others to add remarks or veto a blog post after it is shared, which Noémi Biró added to the organizational agreements page (00:36:50).
unBody Website Structure and Pivot Gabor Kerekes proposed making "lab" the homepage for the website, but Amir Houieh preferred keeping the existing homepage to retain the "unBody" history and community understanding, and instead, adding an explicit sentence about the pivot to focus on "unBody lab" (00:38:15) (00:43:42). The team decided to use the original structure but add a sentence about the focus shifting to the lab (00:45:01). Gabor Kerekes also worked on removing elements like random dots from the design (00:46:04).
Website Aesthetic and Content Strategy The team debated adding unique design elements to the website, such as potentially using ASCII art for blog post headers and having different styles for various pages, drawing inspiration from experimental web designs (00:49:43) (00:52:51). Regarding content, Amir Houieh recommended keeping blog posts about concrete engineering topics while deleting business-related ones, particularly those not linked to YouTube lectures (00:55:53).
Upcoming Tasks and Availability Amir Houieh planned to finish evaluation, work on 'brain,' and outline the agreement for the next phase (00:26:13). Noémi Biró is going through feedback forms, with the next user interview scheduled for the following Thursday (00:58:22). Amir Houieh noted they might be unavailable for a meeting the next day due to travel to Germany (00:58:22).
Suggested next steps
Noémi Biró will go through all the feedback in the form to see how many times the mentioned issues reoccur.
Amir Houieh will start outlining the agreement based on the past conversation and the agreed next phase.
Gabor Kerekes will fix a small bug on the unbody website and refine the gradient presence for both desktop and mobile versions.
Gabor Kerekes will propose a list of articles to keep on the blog, review Amir Houieh's last post to establish a guideline, and provide feedback to Amir Houieh on the dev container.
Gabor Kerekes will update the unbody website to keep the homepage as it is and add a sentence explicitly stating the pivot to focus on unbody lab.
Amir Houieh will push the MCP before traveling to Germany.
Noémi Biró will write the agreement about a 3-day buffer for blog post remarks/vetoes in the organizational/operational agreements page in Notion.
